source_evidence_statements: research/accent-conversion-20261101/README.md records QuickVC / ContentVec as 'Not tested as standalone systems': generic VC architecture/content-encoder components, not a ready-made accent conversion model, with no accent-target checkpoint available; an encoder alone cannot produce converted speech.
plan/INVENTORY.json assigns the voice verification profile to SDK-CONTENTVEC and records the same 'not tested as standalone' finding for contentvec and quickvc.

research/voice-conversion-eval-20261101/repos/rvc is pinned at 81eed5e8 under an MIT LICENSE; its infer/hubert.py loads a transformers HubertModelWithFinalProj from assets/hubert_base and declares v1 = hidden_states[9] through final_proj (256-wide) and v2 = last_hidden_state (768-wide).

assets/hubert_base contains only config.json and preprocessor_config.json; the required pytorch_model.bin is absent. The pinned RVC-MLX consumer instead declares assets/contentvec/pytorch_model.bin and an Applio download URL, and that path is also absent.

The config declares a 768-wide, 12-layer HuBERTModelWithFinalProj with conv_stride [5,2,2,2,2,2,2] (320-sample, 50 Hz content rate), classifier_proj_size 256, torch_dtype float16 and transformers 4.49.0; these are static declarations, not measured behaviour.

No standalone ContentVec timing, feature, content-fidelity, listening, device or release result exists locally; the RVC whole-file pipeline timing is a different system and is not attributed to ContentVec.
